why_angle: The cited rivals say only that the Santa Fe Compact70's pump is 'sold separately' or 'optional'. None gives Santa Fe's own kit part number (4022220) or its limit of 12 ft vertical and 20 ft total. They also quote 19.6 ft as pump lift for AlorAir units whose maker pages give 19.6 ft only as hose length. This page separates the lift each maker actually states from the hose length, which is the deciding fact when the drain is above the unit.

page.desc: Crawl space dehumidifiers with a built-in condensate pump, compared by AHAM capacity, coverage and the pump lift each maker actually states, with prices checked 2026-11-17. Santa Fe's add-on kit for the Compact70 lifts 12 ft.
page.answer: Short answer. The best crawl space dehumidifier with a built-in condensate pump for most crawl spaces is the AlorAir Sentinel HD55P: 55 pints/day (AHAM), 1,300 sq ft, integrated pump plus a 19.6 ft hose. Santa Fe's add-on pump kit for the Compact70 lifts only 12 ft vertically.

What the differences mean

  • Price per AHAM pint/day. HD55P: $583.28 ÷ 55 = $10.61. HDi65S Black WiFi: $595.25 ÷ 55 = $10.82. HD35P WiFi: $438.92 ÷ 35 = $12.54. Abestorm SNS90: $802.98 ÷ 90 = $8.92. HDi90: $1,032.39 ÷ 90 = $11.47.
  • HDi65S over HD55P. $595.25 − $583.28 = $11.97 more buys Wi-Fi (AlorAir-C app) and an ENERGY STAR listing: 2.08 L/kWh and 379 kWh/yr, the only third-party efficiency figure among these units.
  • Cool crawl spaces. The same ENERGY STAR record gives the HDi65S 36.33 pints/day at the DOE test of 65°F / 60% RH, against 55 at AHAM's 80°F. That is 36.33 ÷ 55 = 66%. In a crawl space near 65°F, size the unit for about two-thirds of its AHAM figure.
  • SNS90 vs HDi90. Both list 90 AHAM pints and 2,600 sq ft, and the cabinets are the same size. The SNS90 costs $1,032.39 − $802.98 = $229.41 less and is in stock. AlorAir's warranty runs longer.
  • Small crawl spaces. The HD35P WiFi costs $7.23 more than the plain HD35P ($431.69). The Abestorm Guardian SN35P ($349.58) uses the same 15.2 × 11.2 × 11.4 in cabinet and 19.6 ft pump pipe.

AlorAir's Galaxy 85P (85 AHAM pints, up to 2,300 sq ft) shows as out of stock at $899.11 on alorair.com, so it is not in the table.

Built-in pump vs add-on pump kit: how high the water can go

A built-in condensate pump sits inside the cabinet. Water collects in an internal reservoir, a float starts the pump, and the pump pushes the water up the drain hose to a sink, a sump or a line leaving the house. CrawlSpaceDehumidifiers.org notes that the float also shuts the dehumidifier off if the pump fails. A clogged pump or a drain set too high stops the drying, not just the draining. The same source notes that any horizontal run and elbows reduce the lift you actually get.

Santa Fe's crawl-space units drain by gravity. Santa Fe sells a separate Condensate Pump Kit, part 4022220, which it lists for the Compact70, Ultra70, Ultra98, Ultra120, Ultra155, Ultra205 and others. Santa Fe states that the kit moves water up to 12 ft vertically, with a 20 ft total run and a 2-quart reservoir.

Measure from the floor under the unit to the highest point of the drain line. Under 12 ft, any of these will drain. Over 12 ft, the Santa Fe kit is out, and the HD35P WiFi {buy:alorair-sentinel-hd35p-wifi} is the only unit here with a maker-stated lift above that height. For the HD55P or HDi65S, ask AlorAir to confirm the lift in writing before you rely on that height.

Not recommended

AlorAir Sentinel HDi90 (Built-in Pump), for now. It is widely named the large-crawl-space pick, but alorair.com lists it as out of stock at $1,032.39, and its Wi-Fi version is out of stock too. AlorAir's product page also gives no pump lift figure. The Abestorm Guardian SNS90 lists the same 90 AHAM pints, 2,600 sq ft and cabinet size, plus a stated 14.7 ft drain height, for $229.41 less. Its shorter 1-year full warranty is the trade-off.
